title: Tarte fine aux pommes
subtitle: a thin, crisp French apple tart on puff pastry with thinly sliced apples and a butter glaze
excerpt: Tarte fine aux pommes is a French apple tart made on a thin round of puff pastry covered in overlapping slices of apple, brushed with butter and sugar and baked until the pastry is crisp and the apples are softened and lightly caramelised at the edges. It is one of the simplest tarts to make and one of the most elegant.
sourceNotes: Tarte fine aux pommes is a staple of French home cooking and boulangerie, and appears in canonical texts of French cookery including those of Robuchon and the Larousse Gastronomique. The concept of a very thin pastry base with simply arranged fruit is widely considered the definitive French apple tart alongside the tarte Tatin.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best eaten warm from the oven or within a couple of hours of baking. The pastry softens if left much longer.

content.text: Tarte fine aux pommes is a very thin, very simple French apple tart on a round of puff pastry. The pastry is rolled to a thin disc, covered with overlapping apple slices, brushed with melted butter and sugar, and baked until crisp. The edges of the apple slices catch and colour in the oven while the pastry underneath turns deep golden and shattering. It is made in about 40 minutes from start to table.

items.prepNote: Cox, Braeburn, or similar; peeled, cored, halved

content.text: Heat the oven to 200 degrees C (fan 180 degrees C / gas 6). Line a flat baking tray with baking paper.

Cut the puff pastry sheet into a 30 cm circle or leave as a rectangle; either shape works. Transfer to the lined tray. Use a sharp knife to score a 1 cm border around the edge without cutting through, then prick the inner area all over with a fork. Refrigerate for 15 minutes.

Slice the apple halves as thinly as possible on a mandoline or by hand, about 2 mm thick. Arrange in overlapping rows or a spiral pattern over the inner pastry, leaving the border clear. The slices will shrink as they cook, so pack them fairly tightly.
Mix the melted butter, caster sugar, and vanilla if using. Brush generously over the apple slices.

Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and the apple edges are catching and caramelising. The underside of the pastry should be golden and set. Slide the tart off the paper to check; if the base is still pale, return to the oven on the shelf with nothing underneath for a further 5 minutes.
While still warm, brush with warmed apricot jam for a professional glaze. Leave for 10 minutes before cutting. Serve with cream or creme fraiche.

attrs.problem: Pastry base soft and undercooked in the centre
attrs.avoid: Avoid placing the tray on a high shelf with a lot of top heat; the apples colour before the base cooks through.
attrs.fix: Bake in the middle or lower third of the oven. The fork-pricked base and a hot oven are essential. Checking the underside 5 minutes before the end time prevents disappointment.

attrs.problem: Apple slices curling and falling off the pastry
attrs.avoid: Avoid slicing the apples too thickly; thick slices cannot lie flat and curl as they bake.
attrs.fix: Slice as thinly as possible. A mandoline makes this much easier and more consistent. If slices curl anyway, press them gently back down with a spoon halfway through baking.
